facts.fact: Phil gropes beside the door of the book-lined cellar, finds a light switch and turns it on.
facts.anchor: She groped desperately by the side of the door, hoping for a light switch

facts.fact: Phil opens the biscuit tin on the small table and finds only custard creams inside.
facts.anchor: When Phil nervously opened it, there was nothing but custard creams inside

facts.fact: Examining the shelves, Phil finds every book in the room is about summoning demons.
facts.anchor: they were all about summoning demons

facts.fact: Phil walks across the room to look closely at a tapestry of a woman holding a book and a flame.
facts.anchor: walked across to examine it more closely

facts.fact: Phil steps behind the lectern and starts reading aloud the Latin invocation to Alastor.
facts.anchor: she stepped behind the lectern and began to read

facts.fact: Unable to stop reading, Phil shouts the instruction written in capitals on the page.
Phil passes out and later wakes on a bed in an unfamiliar room.
Matron shines a torch into Phil's eyes and tests her for concussion.
facts.anchor: shining a torch into her eyes

relations.fact: The Head is the person who keeps the secret cellar of demonology books, and Phil is considering whether it is her business to interfere.
relations.anchor: if the Head wanted to keep a secret cellar full of books

relations.fact: Matron treats Phil as a teacher under her authority, calling her a bad teacher and asking whether she is a good or bad teacher.
relations.anchor: No! Bad teacher! No making it worse!

relations.fact: Smithson is the member of staff who found Phil and reported hearing her cat.
relations.anchor: Smithson found you. Said he heard your cat mewing.

relations.fact: The black cat addresses Phil as its mistress, so the cat is hers.

numbers.fact: The rising bell for the girls is at seven; Matron releases Phil at six o'clock.
numbers.anchor: It was six o’clock now, and the rising bell for the girls was at seven

numbers.fact: The biscuit tin is from Queen Elizabeth's Silver Jubilee in the seventies.
numbers.anchor: Silver Jubilee back in the seventies

numbers.fact: Four smaller chairs stand in a half-circle in one part of the cellar.
numbers.anchor: four smaller chairs stood in a more remote half-circle
